A choice now, not a general lack of ability

grammar.note_en:
The polite nonpast negative ends in ません. With the whole forms taught here, replace final ます with ません: のみます → のみません, “drink” → “do not drink”; たべます → たべません, “eat” → “do not eat.” These forms stay the same for Yui, Ren or the shopowner. They are nonpast, so their time comes from the context: いまはのみません means “I am not drinking it now,” not “I did not drink it.” Dictionary forms and past forms are not needed here.

あります means an object exists or is present; its polite negative is ありません. ここにかぎはありません means “There is no key here.” It does not tell us where the key actually is. The animate pair is います / いません: えきにはいません means “The person is not at the station.” Do not use ありません as the ordinary existence verb for a person. The familiar ではありません denies a noun identification: やすみではありません means “It is not a day off/closure.” It is not interchangeable with “no object is present.”

A topic or contrast can be marked by は. おちゃはのみません means “As for tea, I will not drink it.” Yui instead drinks water; she does not reject all drinks. In いえへはいきません, “I will not go to the house,” は follows the direction phrase いえへ. The woman stays at her open shop with customers. This is a present decision or commitment, not a newly taught Japanese potential form meaning “cannot.” There is no general claim that she lacks the ability to leave.

ませんか after an action form can invite someone to join an action: おちゃをのみませんか means “Would you like some tea?” and いっしょにいえへいきませんか means “Would you like to go to the house together?” A negative question can have other functions in Japanese; these contexts make an invitation clear. A response may accept the invitation or explain another choice. Yui thanks the owner and chooses water. The final か is already the question particle: when an exercise supplies it after the gap, do not type a second one.

For a shared proposal or an offer of the speaker’s action, replace ます with ましょう in these taught polite forms. いっしょにたべましょう means “Let’s eat together”; おちゃものみましょう means “Let’s drink tea too.” じゅうしょをわたしましょう means “I’ll give you the address”; わたしもにもつをもちましょう means “I’ll carry the parcel too.” The understood people and practical situation decide between a shared “let’s” and an individual offer. It is not a command or a prediction about every person present.

わたします means hand something over. を marks what changes hands, and に can mark the recipient: じゅうしょのかみをゆいにわたします means “She hands the address card to Yui.” Compare いえでかぎのかかりにあいます, “We will meet the key holder at the house”: に names the person met there. Both are bounded verb patterns here, not a licence to put に after every person. The current prose demonstrates the recipients before practice asks about them.

やすみ here is a closure or day off, a noun: きょうはやすみではありません means “Today is not a day off.” It does not teach a new verb meaning rest. ひと is a person and いえ is a home or house. The address card gives the caretaker’s actual address, but its exact text is not transcribed. The blue entrance and river are separate route clues, not a claim to be a full postal address.

The external parcel label and a captioned reference show まえのなまえ, “former name.” This is a bounded noun phrase; the chapter does not yet teach spatial まえ or clauses meaning “before doing something.” The printed former name is かわのほんのへや, while the current room name is ほんのへや. That evidence identifies the name relationship. It does not establish when or why the name changed. The private letter stays sealed: the characters inspect its outside envelope, not its contents. At the end they return toward Mei, so the proposed home delivery has not yet occurred on the page.

The story adds the kanji spellings of four already known words, using five new characters: いりぐち, あかい, あおい and なか. All story kanji keep authored readings, including the earlier book/name/size spellings. The writing changes; those familiar meanings do not become new vocabulary. Practice and vocabulary labels remain in kana in this phase.

A.title: Pensa A — a statement, an invitation, a proposal

obrazec.rule: New miniature incidents. Cues: 1 invite drinking; 2 does not eat; 3 propose drinking; 4 propose going; 5 absent person; 6 propose handing over; 7 does not look; 8 propose returning. Type the complete polite form before any supplied か. Type kana.
obrazec.prompt: 「めいさん、かわへはいきません。えきへ___。」

items.prompt: 「めいさん、あしたのよる、おちゃを___か。」
ゆいは、きょうのひる、おかしを___。
「れんさん、ここでみずを___。」
「めいさん、あした、いっしょにみせへ___。」
れんのいえに、ゆいは___。
「ゆいさんに、じゅうしょのかみを___。」
めいは、ゆいのふうとうのなかを___。
「れんさん、あしたのよる、いえへ___。」

B.title: Pensa B — useful things and people

obrazec.rule: New miniature incidents. Noun bank: use each answer unchanged. Meaning cues: 1 tea; 2 water; 3 parcel; 4 address; 5 closure/day off; 6 person; 7 letter; 8 sweets. There are three noun extras. Type kana.

items.prompt: 「これは、れんの___です。ゆいのみずではありません。」
ゆいは、いえで___をのみます。
れんの___は、めいのはこのとなりにあります。
ゆいは、かぎのかかりの___をかみにかきます。
「きょうのよるは、みせの___です。」
ゆいは、えきでみせの___にあいます。
めいの___には、ゆいのなまえがあります。
れんとめいは、いえで___をたべます。

C.title: Pensa C — the delivery and its labels

obrazec.rule: Worked example: Mei’s location while the other two are at the shop. Then recall these stages: 1 the shop’s opening small-box inspection; 2 Yui’s drink choice; 3 the woman’s availability; 4 the matched address card and parcel label; 5 the printed former-name reference; 6 the final return decision. Give a complete true sentence. Equivalent answers are welcome; keep sealed contents private.
obrazec.prompt: めいは、どこにいますか。

items.prompt: ふうとうは、どこにありますか。
model_answers: ちいさいはこのなかにあります。
items.rubric: Section 1 opening: the envelope is inside the small box shown by the shopowner. Do not confuse this small box with the later large delivery parcel.

items.prompt: ゆいは、どれをのみますか。
model_answers: ゆいはみずをのみます。
items.rubric: Section 2: Yui declines tea and drinks water. Include the positive water choice; a bare no is insufficient.

items.prompt: みせのひとは、きょう、どこにいますか。
model_answers: みせのひとは、みせにいます。
items.rubric: Sections 1–3: the woman remains at her open shop with customers; she does not accompany the delivery. Do not turn いきません into a general claim that she lacks the physical ability to go.

items.prompt: かぎのかかりのじゅうしょは、どこにありますか。
model_answers: ゆいのかみとにもつのふだにあります。
じゅうしょのかみと、にもつのふだのうらにあります。
items.rubric: Section 3, after the card handover: name the address card now held by Yui and the parcel tag, whose reverse Ren inspects. Both have the same address. Accept equivalent complete location answers; do not invent or require the untranscribed postal-address string.

items.prompt: しゃしんのかみに、まえのなまえがあります。どれですか。
model_answers: かわのほんのへやです。
まえのなまえは、かわのほんのへやです。
items.rubric: Section 4 printed reference: former name かわのほんのへや. The current room label is ほんのへや. This asks about the printed name, not a guess about the date or reason for a change.

items.prompt: ゆいとれんは、どこへかえりますか。
model_answers: ほんのへやへかえります。
ゆいとれんは、ほんのへやへかえります。
items.rubric: Final decision: they return toward the reading room to consult Mei before the home delivery. Ren carries the sealed parcel; Yui carries the sealed letter and address card. No contents are opened or read.

vocabulary.current_sense: sweets; a small snack offered with a drink
earlier; previous, first bounded to まえのなまえ “former name”

notes: Original authored Japanese narrative, notices, captions, diagrams and practice. No authentic quotations, copied teaching sentences, audio or paid raster generation. Four connected acquisition stages retain full 40 workbook +8 A +8 B +6 C responses.

Negative statements, invitations and offers determine the actual delivery decision. Only dated whole surfaces are added; no past, potential, unlicensed plain forms or general numeral series is assumed.

Stable ja-07-03 まえ is introduced in chapter 6 inside its open slots, first bounded to まえのなまえ, rather than duplicating a later semantic ID. The printed reference establishes the former name; it supplies no date or historical event.

The woman uses a distinct char-shopowner speaker ID. Mei stays at the reading room; Ren carries one sealed parcel and Yui one sealed letter, address card and her separate large memo. The two invitation copies remain with Mei. The caretaker’s public posted note stays at the shop.

The exact address is deliberately not transcribed. Abstract writing lines in the delivered address field are separate from the known river/blue-entrance route clues. The characters can compare the full address without readers inferring a municipal addressing system.

The longer English grammar note distinguishes polite negation, invitation and proposal/offer, recipient and meeting-person に, contextual unavailability from potential, and the bounded former-name phrase; it does not substitute for the 2300-atom narrative. Five form notes accompany actual target instances.

Parent adopts the bounded G06 map clarifications for dated negative/invitation/offer forms, recipient/person-metに, contrastiveは after a marked phrase, and former-nameまえ. No potential, past, spatialまえ or unrestricted case paradigm is licensed. The plan’s14new units remain within21. The former-name reference is a full-width inline figure for readable phone delivery; SVGs have title/description metadata.

The house meaning has the delivered English introduction and the river/entrance route context; no figure is claimed to supply a full postal address or depict an unseen house. The media-coverage advisory is retained for independent first-use assessment.

Parent preflight makes the opening key-location request actual direct speech rather than the awkward object phraseかぎをききます; the later proposal asks for an address. The drink-choice C model answers the open which-drink question directly, without an irrelevantいいえ. This adds no new word or grammar allocation.
